title: Adaptable Aerobic Activity
goal: Explore adaptable Aerobic Activity at a comfortable, adaptable level.
readiness: Adult engages in regular baseline aerobic exercise without chest pain or dizziness.
steps: Choose a familiar enjoyable aerobic activity and start easily.
Increase effort only to a personally manageable pace; at moderate intensity you can talk but not sing.
Alternate activity and easy recovery as desired, then finish gradually; no fixed heart-rate zone is required.
completionCriteria: Participant completes a comfortable bout of aerobic movement with a warm-up, rests and cool-down as needed.
safety: Stop for chest pain, faintness or unusual breathlessness and seek medical advice as appropriate.
Start with manageable amounts and build gradually; adapt to health conditions and professional advice.
adaptations: Use shorter attempts, accessible materials or additional support.
Adapt the activity to your language, interests, health and current ability; participation does not require unassisted performance.
benefits: Offers adaptable practice with movement or everyday hand skills. Choose support and effort that feel comfortable.

title: Everyday Aerobic Movement
goal: Try an accessible aerobic activity and choose a feasible routine.
readiness: Choose this when comfortable and interested, using support suited to current ability. No earlier activity completion is required.
steps: Choose enjoyable accessible movement such as walking, wheeling, cycling or seated aerobic activity, and try a short comfortable bout with rests as needed.
Start with a comfortable amount and build gradually toward adult guidance: 150–300 minutes of moderate or 75–150 minutes of vigorous aerobic activity per week.
Include strengthening on at least 2 days; at ages 65 and older also plan balance and strength-focused multicomponent activity on at least 3 days, adapted to ability.
Short bouts can contribute to activity totals; the optional journal session length is not the whole weekly target.
completionCriteria: Participant chooses an accessible activity and a feasible next step without a fitness threshold.
safety: Supervise children closely and use age-appropriate materials with no detachable small parts.
Stop for discomfort, fatigue or disengagement; never force movement or a response.
